title: Introduce One New Chore at a Time | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: Sort, fold, match, carry, and put away can turn one laundry request into a long list of new skills. Expecting a child to learn every step at once can make an ordinary family chore feel overwhelming. Pause and choose one new responsibility that fits the child's age and current ability. Try: Your job today is pairing the socks; demonstrate the first pair, keep the rest visible, and praise honest effort. One clear new task gives the child a realistic chance to build competence before the routine expands.

claim_limits: Suggested wording is an example, not a guaranteed result.
